pl-l2d28c4-d1e108.summary: Concludes with Jerome's exposition of the faith to Damasus, against Jovinian, Mani, and Pelagius: we confess free choice so as to say we always need God's help; those who say with Mani that man cannot avoid sin, and those who say with Jovinian that he cannot sin, both err and remove freedom of choice; we say man can always sin and not sin, and so confess we are always free. This is the faith of the Catholic Church.
claims: Man can always sin and not sin.

pl-l2d28c4.summary: Concludes with Jerome's exposition of the Catholic faith to Pope Damasus, refuting Jovinian, Mani, and Pelagius: we confess free choice so as to say we always need God's help; those who say with Mani that man cannot avoid sin err as much as those who say with Jovinian that man cannot sin; both remove freedom of choice; we say man can always sin and not sin, and so is always free.
claims: It is an error to say man cannot avoid sin.
It is an error to say man cannot sin.
Both errors remove freedom of choice.
Man can always sin and not sin, and so is always free.
